boundary_rationale: This row opens on the messenger frame כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.56.1), which launches the divine command “Maintain justice and do what is right, for my salvation is near and my righteousness will soon be revealed.” (web:Isa.56.1). The command sets the terms for the admission promise that follows: the foreigner who fears being excluded and the eunuch who calls himself “a dry tree” (web:Isa.56.3) are answered by a second, reinforcing instance of the same messenger formula at web:Isa.56.4 (oshb:Isa.56.4), promising those eunuchs “a memorial and a name better than of sons and of daughters” (web:Isa.56.5) and the foreigners a standing “for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.” (web:Isa.56.7). The row holds the general sabbath-and-justice exhortation of web:Isa.56.1-Isa.56.2 together with the foreigner/eunuch oracle of web:Isa.56.3-Isa.56.7 as one admission unit rather than opening a fresh row at the third-person turn of web:Isa.56.3, since no new addressee or frame marker intervenes there and the same messenger frame governs both. The row closes with Isa.56.8, whose divine signature נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.56.8, the adonai-YHWH form) stands verse-initial and heads the gathering clause it introduces -- “I will yet gather others to him, in addition to his own who are gathered.” (web:Isa.56.8) -- rather than closing or sealing it; the formula class is postpositive elsewhere across the book's koh-amar/neum census, but this instance opens its own clause. The row ends the verse just before the addressee shift to the summoned field animals at web:Isa.56.9.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading opens a fresh row at the third-person turn of web:Isa.56.3, treating the sabbath-and-justice exhortation of web:Isa.56.1-Isa.56.2 as a separate short unit from the foreigner/eunuch admission oracle.

device_notes: This row's own front seam Isa.55.13 and its interior verses Isa.56.2, Isa.56.3, and Isa.56.5 each carry setumah breaks (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only, never a driver here). Separately, oshb:Isa.56.4 carries a single paseq seg (count-only, no intra-verse position claimed), an unrelated disclosure class. The messenger frame opening Isa.56.1, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.56.1), and the frame at Isa.56.4, כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.56.4), collate against each other at consonantal-skeleton tier only: the opening letter of the first carries a dagesh that the second lacks, so the two fail even accent-stripped tier, and the Isa.56.4 instance is not itself verse-initial, standing after the subordinating כִּי that opens that verse. Both sit on the divine side of the book-wide koh-amar census (44 of 48 verses per the current inventory classification), not the royal-messenger side confined to 4 sites in the chs 36-37 narrative zone. The unit's real internal cohesion is a byte-identical refrain pair bracketing the third-person turn: שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ (byte tier) recurs between Isa.56.2 and Isa.56.6 (oshb:Isa.56.2, oshb:Isa.56.6), and וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי (byte tier) recurs between Isa.56.4 and Isa.56.6 (oshb:Isa.56.4, oshb:Isa.56.6). Separately, this row's own front seam carries a cross-seam echo: the closing run לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת (byte tier) is shared by the verse just before this row's span, Isa.55.13 (that verse's own ketiv/qere note sits earlier in it, outside the quoted words), and this row's own Isa.56.5 (oshb:Isa.55.13, oshb:Isa.56.5), a byte-identical pair straddling the front boundary, standing at byte tier in exactly two verses book-wide; its consonantal skeleton reaches a third, oshb:Isa.48.19.

boundary_rationale: This row opens where the wayyiqtol narrative chain begins: וַתְּהִ֤י הָֽאֱמֶת֙ נֶעְדֶּ֔רֶת (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.15, byte tier) is itself the chain's first link, continuing directly into וַיַּ֧רְא יְהוָ֛ה וַיֵּ֥רַע בְּעֵינָ֖יו (byte tier) -- “Yahweh saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice.” (web:Isa.59.15) -- and on through “He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head.” (web:Isa.59.17), the chain's last wayyiqtol link, וַיַּ֥עַט כַּמְעִ֖יל קִנְאָֽה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.17) -- “and was clad with zeal as a mantle.” (web:Isa.59.17). The chain does not continue into web:Isa.59.18: its verbs כְּעַ֤ל גְּמֻלוֹת֙ כְּעַ֣ל יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.18) are plain imperfects, "he will repay," not wayyiqtol forms, so the repayment of “wrath to his adversaries” (web:Isa.59.18) is a byte-checkable claim argued from the pointed bytes themselves, not a topical extension of the narrative chain. The row keeps the arrival oracle “A Redeemer will come to Zion, and to those who turn from disobedience in Jacob,” says Yahweh. (web:Isa.59.20), closing on its own postpositive signature נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.20), together with the covenant formula that follows rather than closing there, since Isa.59.21 opens its own distinct frame -- וַאֲנִ֗י זֹ֣את בְּרִיתִ֤י אוֹתָם֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.21, byte tier), carrying the doubled speech frame אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה twice in the verse -- “As for me, this is my covenant with them,” says Yahweh. (web:Isa.59.21) -- and reads as the same divine speaker's continuation on a distinguishable frame object rather than an independent fresh oracle. The row closes at web:Isa.59.21; unlike the seams that bound the book's major frames, this junction sits inside a single parent frame and carries no tier-1 signal of its own -- only a tier-3, single-witness parashah mark -- so the rear boundary is held at reduced confidence rather than argued as a frame seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading closes a row at the postpositive signature of web:Isa.59.20 and opens a fresh covenant-formula row at web:Isa.59.21, since that verse's fronted first-person pronoun and its own doubled 'says Yahweh' frame could stand as an independent unit.

The light-and-rising root standing mid-verse inside this row's own span, וּמִמִּזְרַח שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ (oshb:Isa.59.19), runs on past this row's own rear seam through זָרָֽח (oshb:Isa.60.1, byte tier), יִזְרַ֣ח (oshb:Isa.60.2, byte tier), and זַרְחֵֽךְ (oshb:Isa.60.3, byte tier); the redeemer-and-salvation vocabulary this row's own back half carries also recurs later in the following chapter. Neither is argued as evidence for this row's own boundary; both are disclosed because the seam they cross has no tier-1 warrant of its own.

boundary_rationale: A second-person-feminine-singular imperative pair opens the unit, “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh's glory has risen on you!” (web:Isa.60.1), matching ק֥וּמִי א֖וֹרִי (oshb:Isa.60.1, byte tier). The same addressee is sustained through further imperative and declarative movements — nations and kings drawn to her light, sons and daughters carried home, foreign wealth and foreign service given to her, her gates kept open — without an explicit change of addressee or scene across the chapter. A recognition-formula clause partway through, “Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.” (web:Isa.60.16), matching וְיָדַ֗עַתְּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.60.16, byte tier), is not repeated at the unit's own close: “I, Yahweh, will do this quickly in its time.” (web:Isa.60.22), matching אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּעִתָּ֥הּ אֲחִישֶֽׁנָּה (oshb:Isa.60.22, byte tier), which carries no knowing-verb at all, so the two clauses share only the two-token self-declaration אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ / אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה — a pairing that differs at byte tier and meets from accent-stripped tier down, where it stands in 22 verses book-wide. Even at that lighter tier, the repeated self-declaration frames an internal turn rather than marking a second addressee. Isa.61.1 opens a new first-person speaker frame, “The Lord Yahweh's Spirit is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble.” (web:Isa.61.1), sharing no addressee with this chapter's second-person Zion address, and closes this unit. This row's span is the entirety of chapter 60 (22 verses in the book's own inventory), so under the campaign's whole-chapter rule its confidence is held at the medium_low ceiling rather than assigned a lower band, and that ceiling reflects the span's shape, not any new defect found in it.

device_notes: A setumah (single-witness) marks the parashah layer at oshb:Isa.59.21, immediately before this unit opens, and again at oshb:Isa.60.22, at its own close — tier-3 corroboration for both edges; a paseq (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted) sits at oshb:Isa.60.9, completing the span-relevant symmetry sweep for MT 60.1-60.22 across the parashah, paseq, and ketiv/qere layers. Isa.60.21 stages both the ketiv and qere forms of the planting noun side by side, נֵ֧צֶר מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֖י לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier) — the unpointed ketiv מטעו carries a third-person-masculine-singular suffix ('his planting'), the pointed qere מַטָּעַ֛י a first-person-singular suffix ('my planting'); the two forms differ by suffix person, not number, and this is a single-witness note read either way. The same planting-root vocabulary paired with the 'to be glorified' verb recurs in the following unit's own close (web:Isa.61.3), a catchword this unit's own boundary does not erase. The qadosh-Israel title, a signature title spanning both halves of the book (25 verses swept per attested spelling: 24 at the standard plene spelling, plus the separately-attested defective spelling קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte tier)), recurs at web:Isa.60.9 and web:Isa.60.14 inside this span as in-unit texture, not a boundary driver.

boundary_rationale: A finite third-person-plural clause, “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4), matching וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), opens a report of the community's restoration that continues through an explicit address shift, “But you will be called Yahweh's priests.” (web:Isa.61.6), matching וְאַתֶּ֗ם כֹּהֲנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ תִּקָּרֵ֔אוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier), and a first-person divine declaration, “For I, Yahweh, love justice.” (web:Isa.61.8), matching כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֹהֵ֣ב מִשְׁפָּ֔ט (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier), none of these bringing a vocative or scene marker distinct from the same covenant promise. boundary_rationale: A fresh plural-imperative summons opens the unit, “Go through, go through the gates! Prepare the way of the people!” (web:Isa.62.10), matching עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier). The preceding verses already command an addressed-plural group, the posted watchmen; the turn at this unit's own onset is not a shift to an unnamed addressee but a shift in content, from the charge laid on those watchmen to a highway-preparation summons and, in the following verse, a messenger proclamation, “Behold, Yahweh has proclaimed to the end of the earth:” (web:Isa.62.11), introducing a quoted announcement to Zion. The unit closes on a renaming formula, “They will call them “The Holy People, Yahweh's Redeemed”.” (web:Isa.62.12), matching עַם הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ גְּאוּלֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.62.12, byte tier). This renaming pair brackets the naming clause “You will be called by a new name” (web:Isa.62.2), matching וְקֹ֤רָא לָךְ֙ שֵׁ֣ם חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier), together with the renaming “you will be called Hephzibah” (web:Isa.62.4), matching יִקָּרֵא֙ (oshb:Isa.62.4, byte tier); the recurring niphal form itself, יִקָּרֵא֙ (oshb:Isa.62.4) and יִקָּרֵ֣א (oshb:Isa.62.12), is identical at accent_stripped tier and differs only in cantillation. The renaming bracket this unit's own close completes, once anchored to Isa.62.2 and Isa.62.4, also corroborates a larger reading spanning the whole chapter, bounded at both ends by a tier-3 setumah (single-witness) at oshb:Isa.62.9 and oshb:Isa.62.12; that larger-chapter reading is disclosed rather than adopted here, since web:Isa.62.10 itself opens on a content turn, עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), moving past the charge laid on the watchmen rather than continuing it.

boundary_rationale: The confession turns on a self-accusation standing mid-verse, after the verse's own caesura at יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4, byte tier), whose first half, פָּגַ֤עְתָּ אֶת שָׂשׂ֙ וְעֹ֣שֵׂה צֶ֔דֶק בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4, byte tier), is second-person address continuing the preceding praise: "הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א" (oshb:Isa.64.4, byte tier) (web:Isa.64.5, 'Behold, you were angry, and we sinned'), a first-person-plural admission that has no counterpart in the preceding petition/recollection panel. The unit develops the confession -- “we have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is like a polluted garment” (web:Isa.64.6) -- and moves to a closing series of direct imperative pleas, “Don't be furious, Yahweh. Don't remember iniquity forever.” (web:Isa.64.9), reporting the ruined holy cities and temple (web:Isa.64.10 = oshb:Isa.64.9 through web:Isa.64.11 = oshb:Isa.64.10) before closing on a final unanswered double question, “Will you hold yourself back for these things, Yahweh? Will you keep silent and punish us very severely?” (web:Isa.64.12). The unit ends there because oshb:Isa.65.1 answers this very question with a first-person divine reply, a scene and speaker change that the paragraph-mark inventory also brackets: a SAMEKH break sits at this unit's own close (oshb:Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12).
